open_points.subject: AuditEntry sequence identity after restore
open_points.text: “then one more than the last ever written; never reused” contradicts “A store restored from a backup continues the backup's history, whose last number it continues from” when entries were written after that backup.
open_points.question: After restoring an older backup, may Registry mint sequence numbers that were already minted in the discarded post-backup history, or must it preserve a high-water mark from before the restore?
options: The restored history replaces the discarded branch, so its sequence numbers may be minted again
Sequence numbers are never reused across the store's physical lifetime, so restore must preserve the pre-restore high-water mark
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored backup as the continuing history and allow numbers from the discarded branch to be minted again.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry lifecycle under restore
open_points.text: The lifecycle says “written -> erased by the owner's dated erasure” and “Immutable in between”, while “A store restored from a backup continues the backup's history” makes every entry written after that backup absent without the owner's dated erasure.
open_points.question: Is backup restoration an additional lifecycle event that removes post-backup AuditEntries, or must those entries be preserved or replayed after restoration?
options: Restore rolls the audit log back to the backup and post-backup entries cease to exist in the continuing history
Post-backup entries must be preserved or replayed, leaving dated owner erasure as the only way an entry disappears
open_points.default_guess: Make restoration an explicit rollback exception: post-backup entries are absent from the continuing history.

open_points.subject: One-time import after restoring a pre-import backup
open_points.text: State 0 says “after the first successful import the operation is closed and refused”, while M10 says “A store restored from a backup made before the import continues that backup's history, in which it is absent”.
open_points.question: After a successful import followed by restoration of a pre-import backup, is another import allowed because MigrationClosure is absent, or refused because an import already succeeded during the instance's physical lifetime?
options: The restored history treats the earlier import as not having occurred and permits another import
The one-time closure survives restore outside the backed-up store, so another import is refused
open_points.default_guess: Permit another import because the restored backup defines the continuing store history and contains no MigrationClosure.
